findings.old_behavior: When --negotiation-restrict receives an unresolvable ref name (not a valid object), git dies with error message "%s is not a valid object".
findings.new_behavior: When --negotiation-restrict receives an unresolvable ref name, it is silently ignored (continue). Only missing objects that exist as ref targets still die. The error message for glob patterns that match no refs now shows the option name (--negotiation-restrict) instead of being hardcoded.
findings.compatibility_reason: Scripts or tools that rely on git fetch --negotiation-restrict to fail with a non-zero exit code on invalid ref names will no longer detect the error. This is a silent contract relaxation that could mask user errors or CI misconfiguration.
findings.why_not_internal_only: CLI options --negotiation-restrict and --negotiation-tip are user-facing and documented. Error behavior on invalid input is part of the input contract.
findings.uncertainty: The behavior change only affects the case where an exact ref name does not resolve to a valid object. If the ref name resolves but the object does not exist in the odb, the die() behavior is preserved.
findings.recommended_review: Verify that no internal scripts or CI pipelines rely on git fetch --negotiation-restrict failing on invalid ref names.
findings.test_recommendation: Test that git fetch --negotiation-restrict=invalid-ref no longer exits non-zero, and that it still fails on a valid ref name pointing to a non-existent object.

findings.old_behavior: struct fetch_pack_args has negotiation_restrict_tips as the last field in the pointer-group, occupying a single pointer slot.
findings.new_behavior: struct fetch_pack_args adds negotiation_include_tips (const struct oid_array *) after negotiation_restrict_tips, increasing struct size by one pointer (8 bytes on 64-bit).
findings.compatibility_reason: Any code that embeds struct fetch_pack_args by value or accesses its fields with hardcoded offsets (unlikely in C but possible in FFI/bindings) would break. Normal C code using ->field access is source-compatible.

findings.why_not_internal_only: fetch-pack.h is a public header that defines the struct layout for any code using Git as a library or linking against it.
findings.uncertainty: If all consumers use pointer indirection (struct fetch_pack_args *), the ABI break is limited to sizeof(struct fetch_pack_args) changes in array or stack allocation scenarios.
findings.recommended_review: Review any FFI/binding code that hardcodes struct fetch_pack_args layout.
findings.test_recommendation: Compile test: ensure existing code using struct fetch_pack_args compiles and links correctly.
